title: Typed events: the elegant type that slowed down every call site
question: Does a mapped type with an `as` clause, indexed at every call site, make type-checking measurably slower than inferring the event name from a generic parameter?
verdict: Yes. On an Apple M3 Pro ({{m3.cores}} cores), inferring the event name from the generic parameter cut check time by {{m3.ts6.cut}} with TypeScript 6 and by {{m3.ts7.cut}} with TypeScript 7 ({{m3.ts7.cut.range}} from the fastest and slowest runs); on a {{xeon.cores}}-core Intel Xeon, by {{xeon.ts6.cut}} and {{xeon.ts7.cut}}. The safety check passed on both machines, so the type safety is the same. Narrowing `include` to `src` also stopped TypeScript from reading a generated file the app never imports.
takeaway: A mapped type with an `as` clause is evaluated backwards at each indexed call site. If you can infer the key from a generic instead, the checker does far less work.
notes: Both machines use the earlier protocol: {{m3.runs}} runs per condition, no warm-up, runs in sequence. On the Apple M3 Pro, the runs of TypeScript 7 after the fix vary more than the others ({{m3.ts7.after.min}} to {{m3.ts7.after.max}}, {{m3.ts7.after.cv}} coefficient of variation), hence the wider range on that figure.
The two machines differ by CPU as well as core count: compare the before and after conditions within a machine.
